intent.raw_query: Iceland Northern Lights and hot springs, $3500 couple, January

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunt from Reykjavik
experiences.description: Join a guided minibus tour departing from central Reykjavik to chase the aurora borealis. Expert guides use real-time forecasts to find the clearest skies, often heading toward the Reykjanes Peninsula or Þingvellir area. Includes hot chocolate and photography tips.
experiences.location: Departing from Reykjavik City Centre, Capital Region

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in the iconic milky-blue geothermal waters of the Blue Lagoon, located just 20 minutes from Reykjavik and conveniently near Keflavik Airport. Enjoy silica mud masks, swim-up bars, and steam caves. Book the Comfort package for access to towels and a drink included in the entry.

experiences.name: Golden Circle Day Tour
experiences.description: Explore Iceland's most celebrated natural route covering Þingvellir National Park (a UNESCO World Heritage Site where tectonic plates meet), the erupting Strokkur geyser at Geysir, and the thundering Gullfoss waterfall. Easily accessible from Reykjavik, making it ideal for centrally located travellers.

experiences.name: Snorkeling or Diving in Silfra Fissure
experiences.description: Snorkel or dive between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates in crystal-clear glacial water at Silfra, located within Þingvellir National Park — the same area as the Golden Circle. Visibility exceeds 100 metres in some of the world's purest water. Dry suits are provided. Combine with the Golden Circle for a full day.

experiences.name: Laugardalslaug Geothermal Pool & Local Food at Hlemmur Mathöll
experiences.description: Start your morning with a soak at Laugardalslaug, Reykjavik's largest public geothermal pool complex featuring hot pots, steam rooms, and a waterslide — a true local experience just 2 km from the city centre. Afterward, head to Hlemmur Mathöll food hall for an authentic Icelandic lunch featuring lamb soup, skyr desserts, and fresh seafood from local vendors.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Iceland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrive at Keflavik International Airport at 06:10. Clear customs and collect luggage. Take the Flybus or a budget shuttle to Reykjavik BSI terminal, then arrange onward travel north toward Siglufjörður. The drive is approximately 4-5 hours via Route 1 and the Héðinsfjörður tunnel — consider renting a budget compact car at the airport for the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the scenic drive north through the Tröllaskagi peninsula. Stop briefly at Akureyri if needed for groceries or fuel. Arrive in Siglufjörður in the early afternoon. Check in to Hotel Siglunes on Lækjargata 10 and settle into your room. Take a short recovery walk along the harbor to stretch your legs after the long journey.
day_by_day.evening: Rest and recover from travel. Take a gentle stroll through the quiet, colorful streets of Siglufjörður town center. Keep an eye on the sky after dark — Siglufjörður's low light pollution makes it an excellent spot for northern lights viewing. Check aurora forecast apps (Vedur.is) and step outside around 21:00–23:00 if activity is predicted.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack or coffee at the airport before departure, or pack food from a Keflavik convenience store for the road.
meals.lunch: Pack sandwiches or stop at a Bonus or Krónan supermarket in Akureyri to stock up on budget groceries for the week.
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal using groceries purchased in Akureyri, or try Kaffi Rauðka in Siglufjörður for affordable Icelandic comfort food.

day_by_day.notes: January days in Siglufjörður are very short — expect only about 4–5 hours of daylight. The Héðinsfjörður tunnel (Héðinsfjarðargöng) is toll-free and essential for reaching Siglufjörður. Road conditions can be icy; drive carefully and check road.is before departing.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Herring Era Museum (Síldarminjasafnið) — one of Iceland's most acclaimed regional museums, documenting the herring boom of the early 20th century. It opens at 10:00 in winter. Entry is around 2,000 ISK, making it a worthwhile budget cultural experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the colorful wooden houses and quiet streets of Siglufjörður on foot. Walk along the harbor and out toward the old fish factory ruins. The surrounding snow-capped mountains create a dramatic backdrop. If weather permits, attempt a short hike on the lower slopes above town for panoramic fjord views.
day_by_day.evening: Northern lights watch from the harbor or hillside above town. Siglufjörður is surrounded by mountains that block artificial light, making it ideal for aurora hunting. Bring warm layers, a thermos of hot cocoa, and a tripod if you have a camera. Check Vedur.is for cloud cover and KP index.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered oats or eggs at the hotel using groceries from Akureyri.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch — bread, cheese, and skyr from supermarket supplies.
meals.dinner: Kaffi Rauðka offers hearty soups and fish dishes at reasonable prices. Budget around 2,500–3,500 ISK per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Herring Era Museum may have limited winter hours — confirm opening times by calling ahead or checking their website. Dress in full winter gear for any outdoor activity; temperatures will be near or below freezing.

day_by_day.morning: Drive south along Route 76 to the neighboring village of Hofsós (about 45 minutes). Visit the Icelandic Emigration Center (Vesturfarasetrið), which tells the story of Icelanders who emigrated to North America. Small entry fee, fascinating local history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at the Hofsós infinity swimming pool — one of Iceland's most scenic geothermal pools, perched above the fjord with stunning views of Skagafjörður. Entry is approximately 1,000–1,200 ISK. Soak in the warm geothermal water while gazing at snow-covered mountains across the fjord.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður before dark. Spend the evening aurora hunting from the hillside road above town or from the harbor breakwater. If skies are clear, this is prime northern lights territory.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel — skyr with granola and coffee.
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch from hotel supplies to eat near Hofsós harbor.
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner at hotel — pasta with canned fish or a simple stew using groceries.

day_by_day.notes: Hofsós pool is small and may be closed on certain weekdays in winter — check opening hours at swimiceland.is before going. The road between Siglufjörður and Hofsós is scenic but can be icy; allow extra travel time.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Akureyri (approximately 1.5 hours via the Héðinsfjörður tunnel and Route 1). Explore Iceland's second-largest city on foot. Visit the iconic Akureyrarkirkja church perched on the hill — free entry — and stroll the pedestrian shopping street Hafnarstræti.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Akureyri Botanical Garden (Lystigarðurinn) — free entry and the world's northernmost botanical garden. Though plants are dormant in January, the snow-covered grounds and greenhouse are peaceful. Browse the Bonus supermarket to restock groceries for the week.
day_by_day.evening: Soak at Sundlaug Akureyrar, the city's large geothermal swimming pool complex with hot tubs and steam rooms. Entry is approximately 1,000 ISK — excellent budget value. Return to Siglufjörður after your soak.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel before departure.
meals.lunch: Grab a budget meal at Akureyri's Hlöllabátar (Subway-style sandwich shop) or pick up groceries at Bonus for a picnic.
meals.dinner: Self-catered back at hotel using fresh groceries purchased in Akureyri.

day_by_day.notes: Akureyri has a Bonus, Krónan, and Nettó supermarket — stock up on budget staples like oats, eggs, pasta, canned fish, skyr, and bread. The drive back to Siglufjörður after dark requires extra caution on icy roads.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Tröllaskagi peninsula by car. Drive Route 82 along the eastern side of the peninsula toward Dalvík. Stop at viewpoints overlooking the fjords and mountains. Look for Arctic foxes and ptarmigan in the snowy landscape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Dalvík and its small Byggðasafnið Hvoll folk museum (modest entry fee). Walk along the Dalvík harbor and enjoy views across Eyjafjörður toward the mountains. If time allows, continue to Árskógssandur to see the ferry terminal for Hrísey island.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður via the scenic mountain road (check road conditions first). Aurora watch from the hotel area. The clear mountain air and minimal light pollution around Siglufjörður make every clear evening a potential aurora opportunity.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at a scenic viewpoint along Route 82.
meals.dinner: Kaffi Rauðka or self-catered at hotel.

day_by_day.notes: Route 82 over the Tröllaskagi mountains may be closed or require 4WD in January — always check road.is before setting out. The coastal route via the tunnels is the safer alternative.

day_by_day.morning: Take a winter nature walk in the valley above Siglufjörður. Follow the marked trail toward the old avalanche barriers above town — these massive concrete structures are a reminder of the deadly avalanches that struck Siglufjörður in 1919 and 1920. The walk offers excellent views of the fjord below.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the small Siglufjörður Folk Museum annex buildings near the harbor. Spend time photographing the colorful wooden architecture of the town. Browse any local craft shops that may be open.
day_by_day.evening: Dedicated northern lights photography session. Drive 2–3 km out of town along the fjord road to escape any residual town light. Set up on a safe roadside pullout with a clear view of the sky. The mountains framing the fjord create a spectacular foreground for aurora photos.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered — scrambled eggs and toast.
meals.lunch: Hot soup from a thermos during the morning walk.
meals.dinner: Self-catered hearty stew or pasta at hotel.

day_by_day.notes: January avalanche risk can be elevated after heavy snowfall — do not hike above the avalanche barriers without checking with local authorities. The Icelandic Meteorological Office (Vedur.is) publishes avalanche forecasts.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Skagafjörður. Drive south on Route 76 toward Varmahlíð (about 1.5 hours). Stop at Glaumbær turf farm museum — one of Iceland's best-preserved historic turf farmsteads. Entry is approximately 1,800 ISK and includes a guided look at traditional Icelandic rural life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the Skagafjörður valley floor. Visit the ruins of Hólar Cathedral — historically Iceland's northern episcopal seat and one of the country's most important cultural sites. The current church is small but beautiful, and entry is free. Walk the grounds and explore the historic buildings.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back to Siglufjörður. Stop at a roadside viewpoint on the return journey to check for northern lights. The wide open skies of Skagafjörður offer excellent aurora viewing away from any town lights.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel before departure.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Glaumbær or Hólar.
meals.dinner: Self-catered at hotel or Kaffi Rauðka.

day_by_day.notes: Glaumbær may have reduced winter hours — confirm before visiting. The Skagafjörður valley is known for its Icelandic horse farms; you may spot herds of horses in the snowy fields along the roadside.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and slow morning in Siglufjörður. Sleep in, enjoy a leisurely breakfast, and catch up on rest. Browse the hotel common areas or read. This is a good day to do laundry if facilities are available.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the full length of the Siglufjörður harbor front and explore the outer breakwater. Watch for seabirds including eider ducks and mergansers in the harbor. Visit the small local grocery store to restock any supplies.
day_by_day.evening: Northern lights watch from the harbor. On clear nights, the reflection of the aurora in the calm fjord waters creates a magical double display. Stay out for 1–2 hours if conditions are favorable.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely self-catered breakfast — pancakes or French toast.
meals.lunch: Self-catered light lunch at hotel.
meals.dinner: Treat yourself to a sit-down meal at Kaffi Rauðka — try the fish soup or lamb dish. Budget around 3,000–4,000 ISK.

day_by_day.notes: A rest day is important on a 13-day winter trip in Iceland. The cold, short days and driving can be exhausting. Use this day to recharge before the second half of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Akureyri and take the ferry to Hrísey island (approximately 15 minutes crossing, runs several times daily, very affordable). Hrísey is Iceland's second-largest island and is known for its large population of ptarmigan. Walk the marked trails across the island.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Hrísey village and its small harbor. The island is almost entirely free of cars, making it a peaceful escape. Look for ptarmigan in the low scrub vegetation — they are often remarkably tame in winter. Return ferry to Árskógssandur and drive back toward Siglufjörður.
day_by_day.evening: Aurora watch on the drive back north — pull over at any dark, safe location with a clear northern horizon. The area around Ólafsfjörður is particularly good for aurora viewing.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel before departure.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on Hrísey island — eat at a scenic harbor bench.
meals.dinner: Self-catered at hotel.

day_by_day.notes: Check the Hrísey ferry schedule at hrisey.is before going. The island has very limited services in winter — bring all food and water you need. Dress warmly as the island is exposed to wind.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Mývatn (approximately 2 hours from Siglufjörður via Akureyri and Route 1 east). Arrive at Lake Mývatn and begin exploring the volcanic landscape. Visit Dimmuborgir — a surreal field of lava formations and caves, free to enter and walk through.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Mývatn Nature Baths (Jarðböðin við Mývatn) — Iceland's northern equivalent of the Blue Lagoon but far less crowded and more affordable at approximately 5,500 ISK. Soak in the milky blue geothermal lagoon surrounded by volcanic landscape. Also visit the Hverfjall tephra crater rim (short hike, free).
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward Akureyri and then to Siglufjörður. The Mývatn area has very dark skies — if aurora activity is predicted, stop on the return journey for viewing. Arrive back in Siglufjörður late evening.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered early breakfast before the long drive.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Dimmuborgir or near the lake.
meals.dinner: Self-catered late dinner at hotel after return.

day_by_day.notes: This is a long day with significant driving — approximately 4 hours total. Start early to maximize daylight at Mývatn. The Mývatn Nature Baths are one of the best budget hot spring experiences in Iceland. Book online in advance to guarantee entry.

day_by_day.morning: Recovery morning after the long Mývatn day. Slow start with a warm breakfast. Take a short walk along the Siglufjörður fjord road in the morning light (sunrise around 11:00 in January). Photograph the dramatic mountain reflections in the fjord.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Ólafsfjörður (about 20 minutes through the Strákagöng tunnel). Explore this small fishing village, walk the harbor, and visit the local swimming pool for a warm soak. The Ólafsfjörður pool is small, local, and very affordable (around 900–1,000 ISK).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður. Final dedicated aurora hunting session — set up at the best dark spot you've identified during the trip. January offers long nights (nearly 20 hours of darkness) maximizing aurora viewing windows.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered leisurely breakfast.
meals.lunch: Self-catered packed lunch or eat at a small café in Ólafsfjörður if open.
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner at hotel — use up remaining groceries creatively.

day_by_day.notes: The Strákagöng tunnel connecting Siglufjörður and Ólafsfjörður is free and makes the two towns easily accessible to each other. Ólafsfjörður is a charming, very quiet village worth a brief visit.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Siglufjörður. Take a last walk through the town, revisit favorite spots, and photograph the harbor in the soft winter light. Visit the Herring Era Museum gift shop for any small souvenirs (postcards are very affordable).
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the drive south toward Reykjavik or toward the airport area, depending on your departure logistics. The drive from Siglufjörður to Reykjavik is approximately 5–6 hours. Stop in Akureyri for a final hot pool visit at Sundlaug Akureyrar or a coffee break.
day_by_day.evening: Continue south on Route 1. Stop at Goðafoss waterfall (free, just off Route 1) — even in winter the partially frozen waterfall is spectacular. Arrive in the Reykjavik area and check into a budget guesthouse or hostel near the airport (e.g., Keflavik area) for the final night.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered final breakfast at Hotel Siglunes.
meals.lunch: Stop at a petrol station or Akureyri supermarket for a budget road lunch.
meals.dinner: Budget guesthouse area in Reykjavik/Keflavik — try a Subway, a supermarket hot food counter, or a local pizza place. Budget 2,000–3,000 ISK.

day_by_day.notes: Check out of Hotel Siglunes by the stated checkout time. Goðafoss is accessible year-round and is just a short detour off Route 1 near Fosshóll — do not miss it. Road conditions on Route 1 in January can be challenging; allow extra travel time and check road.is.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Iceland. If your flight departs from Keflavik, allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for check-in and security. Spend any remaining ISK at the airport duty-free or grab a final Icelandic skyr or pastry at an airport café.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart Iceland. Reflect on 13 days of northern lights, geothermal hot springs, volcanic landscapes, and the unique magic of Iceland's remote north in winter.
day_by_day.evening: In transit or arrived at destination.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the guesthouse or airport café — budget around 1,500 ISK.
meals.lunch: Airport meal or in-flight.
meals.dinner: In transit.

day_by_day.notes: Return your rental car at Keflavik Airport with a full tank of fuel (fill up at the last petrol station before the airport to avoid expensive airport fuel prices). Keep all receipts for any potential insurance claims. The Flybus from Reykjavik BSI to the airport runs regularly and is the most budget-friendly transfer option at around 3,500 ISK.

trip_options.title: Classic Iceland Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

Afterward, head to Hlemmur Mathöll food hall for an authentic Icelandic lunch featuring lamb soup, skyr desserts, and fresh seafood from local vendors.

day_by_day.morning: Arrive at Keflavik International Airport at 06:10. Clear customs and collect luggage. Take the Flybus or rent a car toward Reykjavik. Check into a transit guesthouse or use luggage storage to freshen up. Given the very early arrival and long drive north ahead, spend the morning resting and exploring central Reykjavik on foot — stroll around Tjörnin pond, visit Hallgrímskirkja church exterior, and warm up in a café.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa (pre-booked, located 20 minutes from Keflavik — ideal to stop en route before heading north). Soak in the iconic milky-blue geothermal waters, enjoy the steam rooms and silica mud masks. This is a perfect way to recover from the overnight flight. Afterward, begin the scenic drive north toward Siglufjörður (approximately 4–5 hours via Route 1 and the Héðinsfjörður tunnel).
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Hotel Siglunes in Siglufjörður by early evening. Check in, unpack, and settle into this charming fishing village. Take a short walk along the harbor to get oriented. Keep an eye on the sky after dark — January offers excellent northern lights conditions. Check aurora forecast apps (Vedur.is) and step outside if activity is predicted.

meals.breakfast: Grab a pastry and coffee at a Reykjavik café such as Brauð & Co before departing — budget around 1,500–2,000 ISK
meals.lunch: Light meal at the Blue Lagoon's LAVA Restaurant or grab a soup and sandwich from their café counter — budget around 3,000–4,500 ISK
meals.dinner: Dinner at Hannes Boy restaurant in Siglufjörður, a beloved local spot known for fresh fish and hearty Icelandic dishes — budget around 4,000–6,000 ISK

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book the Blue Lagoon well in advance as slots sell out. Ensure your rental car is 4WD for winter driving in northern Iceland. Download the 112 Iceland safety app and register your travel plan. Dress in warm layers — temperatures around 5°C with potential wind chill.

day_by_day.morning: After a good night's rest, explore Siglufjörður on foot in the morning. Visit the award-winning Herring Era Museum (Síldarminjasafnið), which tells the fascinating story of Iceland's herring boom. The museum is one of the best maritime museums in the country and offers great insight into local history. Stroll the colorful harbor and take in the dramatic fjord scenery surrounded by snow-capped mountains.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive the scenic Tröllaskagi peninsula route (Route 76) southward toward Hofsós and Sauðárkrókur. Stop at Hofsós Infinity Pool — a stunning geothermal swimming pool perched on a cliff overlooking Skagafjörður fjord, one of Iceland's most scenic hot pools. Soak and enjoy the panoramic winter views. Continue exploring the area before returning to Siglufjörður via the tunnel.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður by late afternoon. After dinner, join a self-guided northern lights watch from the hotel or nearby dark spots outside town. The fjord location with minimal light pollution makes it excellent for aurora viewing. Bring a thermos of hot chocolate and a tripod if you have a camera.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Hotel Siglunes — typically included or available for a modest supplement. Enjoy skyr, eggs, and Icelandic bread
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch from a local grocery store (Krónan or Nettó) in Siglufjörður — sandwiches, fruit, and hot soup from a thermos — budget around 1,500 ISK
meals.dinner: Dinner at Kaffi Rauðka in Siglufjörður, a cozy café-restaurant with homemade soups, lamb dishes, and local fish — budget around 3,500–5,500 ISK

day_by_day.notes: Hofsós pool is open year-round but check winter hours (typically 10:00–21:00). Bring a swimsuit and towel. The drive along Tröllaskagi is stunning but take care on icy roads — allow extra time. Aurora forecast: check Vedur.is each evening.

day_by_day.morning: Drive south from Siglufjörður to Akureyri (approximately 1 hour via the Ólafsfjörður tunnel). Akureyri is Iceland's second-largest city and a wonderful base for a day trip. Explore the charming town center — visit the Akureyri Botanical Garden (free entry, beautiful even in winter), and walk up to Akureyrarkirkja church for panoramic views over the fjord.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Akureyri Swimming Pool (Sundlaug Akureyrar), a beloved local geothermal pool complex with hot tubs, steam rooms, and a waterslide — a perfect mid-range activity beloved by locals. Afterward, browse the small boutique shops and galleries along Hafnarstræti street. Visit the Akureyri Art Museum if time allows.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner in Akureyri before driving back to Siglufjörður. Alternatively, if aurora activity is forecast to be high, find a dark spot outside Akureyri or along the drive back for northern lights viewing. The mountain roads offer spectacular dark skies.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Hotel Siglunes before departing
meals.lunch: Lunch at Bautinn restaurant in Akureyri — a classic Icelandic diner serving lamb soup, fish and chips, and burgers at reasonable prices — budget around 2,500–4,000 ISK
meals.dinner: Dinner at Strikið restaurant in Akureyri — panoramic fjord views, excellent fish and lamb dishes — budget around 5,000–7,500 ISK

day_by_day.notes: Akureyri is approximately 1 hour from Siglufjörður. The tunnel through Ólafsfjörður makes the drive straightforward. Parking in Akureyri town center is free for the first hour. Bring your swimsuit for the pool visit.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to the Mývatn region (approximately 1.5 hours east of Akureyri via Route 1). Begin at the Mývatn Nature Baths — Iceland's lesser-known but equally stunning geothermal lagoon, often called the 'Blue Lagoon of the North.' Soak in the mineral-rich, silica-blue waters surrounded by volcanic landscape. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon and equally beautiful.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the extraordinary volcanic landscape around Lake Mývatn. Visit Dimmuborgir lava formations (dramatic black lava pillars and arches), the Skútustaðagígar pseudocraters (UNESCO-listed), and Hverfjall volcanic crater rim walk if conditions allow. The surreal, otherworldly scenery is unlike anywhere else on Earth.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward Siglufjörður via Akureyri. Stop for dinner in Akureyri or pick up supplies. Once back at the hotel, check aurora forecasts — the Mývatn area and the drive back offer excellent dark sky opportunities if you time your return for after dark.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Hotel Siglunes before the drive
meals.lunch: Lunch at Vogafjós Farm Restaurant near Mývatn — famous for fresh geothermal bread baked underground, homemade skyr, and farm-fresh meals — budget around 3,000–5,000 ISK
meals.dinner: Dinner at Greifinn restaurant in Akureyri on the way back — pizza and pasta in a relaxed setting, great value — budget around 2,500–4,000 ISK

day_by_day.notes: Mývatn Nature Baths entry is approximately 6,500 ISK per adult — book online in advance. Dress in full winter gear for the outdoor lava field walks. Dimmuborgir and pseudocrater walks are free. Total driving for the day is approximately 3–3.5 hours — start early.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a slower morning in Siglufjörður. Sleep in after the busy previous days. Take a leisurely walk along the harbor and up into the lower mountain slopes above town for views over the fjord. In winter, the surrounding mountains are blanketed in snow and the light (when it appears) is magical. Visit the local swimming pool (Sundlaug Siglufjarðar) for a relaxing morning soak in the hot tubs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Hofsós (approximately 45 minutes south) and continue to Sauðárkrókur, the main town of Skagafjörður. Explore the local area, visit the Skagafjörður Heritage Museum to learn about the region's horse-breeding culture and Viking history. Browse the small town and pick up any supplies needed.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður for a quiet evening. This is a great night to focus on northern lights hunting — set an alarm for midnight if the KP index rises. The hotel can advise on local dark spots. Alternatively, enjoy a cozy evening at the hotel with a book and local beer.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast at Hotel Siglunes
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local bakery or café in Sauðárkrókur — try Kaffi Krókur for homemade soup and fresh bread — budget around 1,500–2,500 ISK
meals.dinner: Dinner at Hannes Boy in Siglufjörður — try the catch of the day or the lamb stew — budget around 4,000–6,000 ISK

day_by_day.notes: The Siglufjörður swimming pool is a wonderful local experience — entry is very affordable (around 1,000 ISK). This is a good rest day to recharge before more active days ahead. Check road conditions before driving to Sauðárkrókur.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Varmahlíð in Skagafjörður valley (approximately 1 hour from Siglufjörður). Visit the Glaumbær Turf Farm Museum — one of Iceland's best-preserved historic turf farmhouses, offering a fascinating glimpse into traditional Icelandic rural life from the 18th and 19th centuries. The site is atmospheric and photogenic in winter snow.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the Reykir Geothermal Area near Varmahlíð. Visit the Reykir swimming pool — a wonderful local geothermal pool with hot tubs fed by natural hot springs. This is a very local, authentic experience far from tourist crowds. Afterward, explore the Skagafjörður valley, known as Iceland's horse country — you may spot Icelandic horses in the snowy fields.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður. Enjoy a quiet dinner and another northern lights watch. January evenings in northern Iceland offer up to 18 hours of darkness — ideal aurora conditions when skies are clear.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Hotel Siglunes
meals.lunch: Lunch at Gilsstaðir Guesthouse café near Varmahlíð — homemade Icelandic food in a farm setting — budget around 2,000–3,500 ISK
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal using groceries from Siglufjörður's local store, or dine at Kaffi Rauðka — budget around 3,000–5,000 ISK

day_by_day.notes: Glaumbær is open in winter but with reduced hours — check ahead (typically 10:00–17:00). The Reykir pool is a hidden gem beloved by locals. Bring your swimsuit. The Skagafjörður valley is one of Iceland's most scenic inland areas.

day_by_day.morning: Drive west along the Snæfellsnes Peninsula direction — but first, head toward Blönduós (approximately 1.5 hours from Siglufjörður). Visit the Textile Museum (Heimilisiðnaðarsafnið) in Blönduós, which celebrates Iceland's rich tradition of wool and textile crafts. Browse the small town and pick up supplies for the day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue west to the Vatnsnes Peninsula (approximately 30 minutes from Blönduós). Visit Hvítserkur — a dramatic 15-meter basalt rock stack rising from the sea, resembling a rhinoceros or dragon. In winter, the surrounding landscape is stark and beautiful. Explore the peninsula for seal spotting at Illugastaðir (harbor seals are often visible year-round on the rocks).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður via the Ring Road. The drive back offers beautiful fjord scenery. Check aurora forecasts for the evening — the open landscapes of the north offer excellent viewing. Arrive back at the hotel for dinner and rest.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Hotel Siglunes before the early departure
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch or stop at a petrol station café along Route 1 — Icelandic petrol station food (pylsur hot dogs, soup) is surprisingly good and budget-friendly — budget around 1,000–2,000 ISK
meals.dinner: Dinner at Hannes Boy or Kaffi Rauðka in Siglufjörður — budget around 4,000–6,000 ISK

day_by_day.notes: Hvítserkur is accessible via a short walk from a parking area — wear waterproof boots as the path can be muddy or icy. Seal spotting at Illugastaðir is free. Total driving today is approximately 3–4 hours — start early to make the most of the limited daylight (roughly 5–6 hours in January).

day_by_day.morning: Begin the drive south toward Reykjavik (approximately 4.5–5 hours from Siglufjörður). Stop at Hraunfossar and Barnafoss waterfalls near Borgarnes — a stunning series of waterfalls where water seeps through ancient lava fields directly into the Hvítá river. The winter ice formations make this particularly magical. Also visit Deildartunguhver, Europe's most powerful hot spring, nearby.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue south and stop at Borgarnes Settlement Center — an excellent interactive museum about the Viking Age settlement of Iceland, based on the Egils Saga. Well worth 1–2 hours. Afterward, continue the drive toward Reykjavik, arriving in the late afternoon. Check into a mid-range guesthouse or hotel in Reykjavik for the remaining nights (e.g., Guesthouse Butterfly or similar).
day_by_day.evening: Explore Reykjavik's vibrant Laugavegur street in the evening. Browse shops, galleries, and bars. This is a great night to experience Reykjavik's famous nightlife or simply enjoy a cozy dinner in the city center.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at Hotel Siglunes
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Settlement Center café in Borgarnes — excellent lamb soup and Icelandic bread — budget around 2,500–3,500 ISK
meals.dinner: Dinner at Messinn restaurant in Reykjavik — famous for their cast-iron pan fish dishes, excellent value — budget around 5,000–7,000 ISK

day_by_day.notes: This is a travel-heavy day — start by 08:00 to maximize daylight for the waterfall stops. Hraunfossar and Barnafoss are free to visit with a small parking fee. Book Reykjavik accommodation in advance. The Settlement Center entry is approximately 2,200 ISK per adult.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with a soak at Laugardalslaug, Reykjavik's largest public geothermal pool complex. Enjoy the outdoor hot tubs, steam rooms, and lap pools alongside locals — a quintessential Icelandic morning experience. Entry is very affordable (around 1,100 ISK). Afterward, visit the nearby Reykjavik Botanical Garden and Húsdýragarðurinn (family zoo and park) for a pleasant walk.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Hlemmur Mathöll food hall — Reykjavik's vibrant street food market in a converted bus terminal. Sample dishes from various vendors including Icelandic lamb, seafood, vegan options, and craft beer. Browse the Laugavegur shopping street and visit the Reykjavik Art Museum (Kjarvalsstaðir branch) nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Join a Northern Lights Hunt guided minibus tour departing from central Reykjavik. Expert guides use real-time aurora forecasts to chase clear skies and find the best viewing spots outside the city. Tours typically run 21:00–01:00 and include aurora photography tips. This is one of the best ways to maximize your chances of seeing the lights.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at Brauð & Co bakery on Frakkastígur — Iceland's most beloved bakery, famous for their cinnamon rolls and sourdough — budget around 1,500–2,000 ISK
meals.lunch: Lunch at Hlemmur Mathöll food hall — try multiple vendors for a varied Icelandic food experience — budget around 2,500–4,000 ISK
meals.dinner: Early dinner before the aurora tour at Sægreifinn (The Sea Baron) — famous for lobster soup and grilled fish skewers, excellent value — budget around 2,500–4,000 ISK

day_by_day.notes: Book the Northern Lights Hunt tour in advance (approximately 9,900–12,000 ISK per person). Most tours offer a free rebooking if aurora activity is too low. Laugardalslaug opens at 06:30 on weekdays and 08:00 on weekends. Bring a swimsuit and towel.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Golden Circle Day Tour — Iceland's most celebrated natural route. Begin at Þingvellir National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates meet and Iceland's ancient parliament was founded. Walk the Almannagjá rift valley and enjoy the dramatic winter landscape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Golden Circle to the Geysir Geothermal Area — watch Strokkur geyser erupt every 5–10 minutes shooting boiling water 20–30 meters into the air. Then visit the majestic Gullfoss waterfall, partially frozen in winter and absolutely spectacular. The Golden Circle can be done as a self-drive or guided tour.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Reykjavik by early evening. Enjoy a relaxed dinner in the city. If aurora activity is forecast, take a short drive outside the city or join another aurora hunt. Alternatively, visit the Perlan museum for its excellent Northern Lights planetarium show.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Reykjavik guesthouse or a nearby café
meals.lunch: Lunch at Geysir Center café near Strokkur — lamb soup and sandwiches — budget around 2,500–3,500 ISK
meals.dinner: Dinner at Fiskmarkaðurinn (Fish Market) in Reykjavik — creative Icelandic-Asian fusion seafood in a mid-range setting — budget around 6,000–9,000 ISK

day_by_day.notes: Self-driving the Golden Circle takes approximately 6–7 hours including stops. A guided tour costs approximately 8,000–12,000 ISK and includes transport. Þingvellir entry is free; parking fee applies. Dress in full winter gear — wind chill at Gullfoss can be intense.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Snorkeling or Diving in Silfra Fissure at Þingvellir National Park (approximately 45 minutes from Reykjavik). Snorkel or dive between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates in crystal-clear glacial water with visibility up to 100 meters. The water is a constant 2–4°C but dry suits keep you warm. This is a bucket-list experience unlike anything else on Earth.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Silfra experience, explore more of Þingvellir National Park on foot. Walk the Öxará river trail and visit the historic Þingvellir church and farmstead. The park is beautiful in winter with snow and ice. Return to Reykjavik by mid-afternoon and warm up with a hot drink.
day_by_day.evening: Spend the evening exploring Reykjavik's cultural scene. Visit the Harpa Concert Hall for a performance or simply admire the stunning glass architecture. Walk along the old harbor and visit the Sun Voyager sculpture. Enjoy a final evening stroll along Laugavegur.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your guesthouse before the Silfra tour departure
meals.lunch: Pack a thermos of hot soup and snacks for after the snorkeling — you'll be hungry and cold. Alternatively, stop at the Þingvellir visitor center café — budget around 1,500–2,500 ISK
meals.dinner: Dinner at Grillmarkaðurinn (Grill Market) in Reykjavik — excellent Icelandic lamb and seafood on a wood-fired grill — budget around 6,000–9,000 ISK

day_by_day.notes: Silfra snorkeling tours cost approximately 19,000–25,000 ISK per person and must be booked well in advance. Dry suits are provided. You must be a confident swimmer. The water is extremely cold — follow all guide instructions. This is one of the top 10 dive sites in the world.

day_by_day.morning: Spend a final full morning exploring Reykjavik's museums and culture. Visit the National Museum of Iceland (Þjóðminjasafn Íslands) for a comprehensive overview of Icelandic history from settlement to modern times — excellent exhibits and very affordable entry. Afterward, walk to the iconic Hallgrímskirkja church and take the elevator to the top of the tower for panoramic city views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Perlan Museum — a stunning glass dome building on Öskjuhlíð hill with exhibits on Iceland's natural wonders including glaciers, volcanoes, and geothermal energy. The Northern Lights planetarium show here is excellent for those who haven't seen the aurora in person. Enjoy the 360-degree observation deck views over Reykjavik.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Reykjavik — treat yourself to a special dinner. Explore the Grandi harbor district, which has become Reykjavik's hippest neighborhood with excellent restaurants, the Marshall House art gallery, and the Reykjavik Street Food market. End the evening with a craft beer at a local bar on Laugavegur.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast at a Reykjavik café — try Café Babalu on Skólavörðustígur for a cozy, bohemian atmosphere — budget around 1,500–2,500 ISK
meals.lunch: Lunch at Reykjavik Street Food (Tryggvagata) — excellent lamb soup, fish stew, and skyr dessert at very reasonable prices — budget around 2,000–3,000 ISK
meals.dinner: Splurge dinner at Dill Restaurant — Iceland's only Michelin-starred restaurant, celebrating New Nordic cuisine with Icelandic ingredients — budget around 15,000–20,000 ISK per person for the tasting menu (book months in advance)

day_by_day.notes: Perlan Museum entry is approximately 4,990 ISK per adult. The Northern Lights show runs several times daily. Hallgrímskirkja tower entry is approximately 1,000 ISK. If budget is a concern, skip Dill and enjoy a final dinner at Messinn or Sægreifinn instead. Pack your bags tonight for the early departure tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Iceland. Depending on your departure flight time, enjoy a last Icelandic breakfast and a final walk along the Reykjavik harbor. Visit the Kolaportið flea market (open weekends — if applicable) for last-minute souvenirs including Icelandic wool products, vintage items, and local food. Pick up duty-free Icelandic spirits, chocolate, and skyr at the airport.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Keflavik International Airport (approximately 45 minutes from Reykjavik by Flybus or rental car return). Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for check-in, security, and duty-free shopping. Reflect on an incredible 13 days exploring Iceland's northern lights, geothermal wonders, and dramatic nature.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Iceland with unforgettable memories of the aurora borealis, steaming hot springs, volcanic landscapes, and the warmth of Icelandic hospitality.

meals.breakfast: Final Icelandic breakfast — enjoy skyr with berries, smoked salmon on rye bread (rúgbrauð), and strong coffee at your guesthouse or a nearby café — budget around 1,500–2,500 ISK
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Keflavik Airport — Icelandic airport food is reasonably priced with good options including lamb soup and sandwiches — budget around 2,500–4,000 ISK
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or at your destination

day_by_day.notes: Return your rental car with a full tank — petrol stations near the airport include N1 and Orkan. The Flybus from BSÍ terminal in Reykjavik to Keflavik runs regularly and costs approximately 3,500 ISK. Allow extra time in winter for potential road delays. Keep your warmest layers accessible until you board the plane.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Iceland Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunt from Reykjavik
experiences.description: Join a guided minibus tour departing from central Reykjavik to chase the aurora borealis. Expert guides use real-time forecasts to find the clearest skies, often heading toward the Reykjanes Peninsula or Þingvellir area. Includes hot chocolate and photography tips.
experiences.location: Departing from Reykjavik City Centre, Capital Region

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in the iconic milky-blue geothermal waters of the Blue Lagoon, located just 20 minutes from Reykjavik and conveniently near Keflavik Airport. Enjoy silica mud masks, swim-up bars, and steam caves. Book the Comfort package for access to towels and a drink included in the entry.

experiences.name: Golden Circle Day Tour
experiences.description: Explore Iceland's most celebrated natural route covering Þingvellir National Park (a UNESCO World Heritage Site where tectonic plates meet), the erupting Strokkur geyser at Geysir, and the thundering Gullfoss waterfall. Easily accessible from Reykjavik, making it ideal for centrally located travellers.

experiences.name: Snorkeling or Diving in Silfra Fissure
experiences.description: Snorkel or dive between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates in crystal-clear glacial water at Silfra, located within Þingvellir National Park — the same area as the Golden Circle. Visibility exceeds 100 metres in some of the world's purest water. Dry suits are provided. Combine with the Golden Circle for a full day.

experiences.name: Laugardalslaug Geothermal Pool & Local Food at Hlemmur Mathöll
experiences.description: Start your morning with a soak at Laugardalslaug, Reykjavik's largest public geothermal pool complex featuring hot pots, steam rooms, and a waterslide — a true local experience just 2 km from the city centre. Afterward, head to Hlemmur Mathöll food hall for an authentic Icelandic lunch featuring lamb soup, skyr desserts, and fresh seafood from local vendors.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Keflavik International Airport at 06:10. Clear customs and collect luggage. A pre-arranged luxury private transfer (Mercedes V-Class or similar) awaits to whisk you directly to the Blue Lagoon, only 20 minutes from the airport — the perfect way to decompress after a long-haul flight. Enjoy a premium 'Retreat Spa' package at the Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa: soak in the iconic milky-blue 38–40°C silica-rich waters, enjoy an in-water algae mask ritual, and relax in the exclusive Retreat lounge.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Blue Lagoon, your private driver continues the scenic 50-minute journey into Reykjavik. Check in early (if possible) or store luggage at a luxury Reykjavik city hotel for the night before the long drive north tomorrow. Spend the afternoon exploring the compact, walkable city centre: visit Hallgrímskirkja church, stroll Laugavegur shopping street for Icelandic wool and design goods, and browse the Reykjavik Art Museum.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunt from Reykjavik: Join an expert-guided premium minibus aurora tour departing central Reykjavik. Guides use real-time cloud and solar activity data to chase clear skies. Wrap up in provided blankets and enjoy hot cocoa while waiting for the aurora borealis to dance overhead.

meals.breakfast: Complimentary light refreshments and Skyr parfait at the Blue Lagoon Retreat Lounge upon arrival
meals.lunch: LAVA Restaurant at the Blue Lagoon — floor-to-ceiling geothermal views, Icelandic lamb soup and pan-seared Arctic char
meals.dinner: Dill Restaurant, Reykjavik — Iceland's first Michelin-starred restaurant; Nordic tasting menu featuring foraged herbs, langoustine, and skyr dessert (advance reservation essential)

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally kept in and around Reykjavik given the early 06:10 arrival. The long drive to Siglufjörður (approx. 5–6 hours) is scheduled for Day 2 when you are rested. Pack warm layers — January temperatures average 5°C with wind chill. Aurora probability is highest after midnight; tour typically returns by 01:00.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, depart Reykjavik by private luxury 4WD vehicle (pre-booked with a professional driver-guide) for the scenic drive north to Siglufjörður — approximately 5.5 to 6 hours including stops. En route, stop at Glymur Waterfall trailhead viewpoint (Iceland's second-tallest waterfall at 198 m) for dramatic winter photography. Continue north through the Hvalfjörður tunnel and along the Snæfellsnes peninsula coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the drive north through Borgarnes and Varmahlíð. Stop at Glaumbær Turf Farm Museum (open limited winter hours) — a beautifully preserved 18th-century turf farmstead offering a window into Viking-age Icelandic life. Enjoy the stark, snow-dusted highland landscapes as you approach the Tröllaskagi peninsula.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Hotel Siglunes in Siglufjörður by late afternoon. Check in and settle into your room overlooking the fjord. Siglufjörður is one of Iceland's most remote and atmospheric small towns, nestled between steep snow-capped mountains. Take a short evening stroll along the harbour front to watch the last light fade over the fjord.

meals.breakfast: Full Icelandic breakfast at your Reykjavik hotel — smoked salmon, skyr, rye bread, and Icelandic cheeses
meals.lunch: Packed premium picnic lunch prepared by the hotel or stop at Café Karolína in Borgarnes — homemade soups and fresh-baked bread
meals.dinner: Sigló Hótel Restaurant (a short walk from Hotel Siglunes) — locally caught Arctic char, lamb shank, and Icelandic craft beer; alternatively dine in-house at Hotel Siglunes if they offer evening service

day_by_day.notes: Road conditions in January can be challenging — ensure your driver has a 4WD vehicle with winter tyres. Check road.is for live updates. The Héðinsfjörður tunnel (opened 2010) makes Siglufjörður accessible year-round. Arrive before dark (sunset around 16:00 in January) for the most scenic final approach through the mountain tunnel.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for a guided snowshoe hike on the lower slopes above Siglufjörður with a local mountain guide. The town is surrounded by dramatic peaks rising to over 1,000 m. In winter, the mountains glow with alpenglow at sunrise (around 11:00 in January). The hike offers sweeping views over the fjord and the colourful fishing village below. Duration approximately 2–3 hours at a leisurely pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the award-winning Herring Era Museum (Síldarminjasafnið) — one of Iceland's finest regional museums, spread across three renovated harbour buildings. It tells the fascinating story of the 'Herring Adventure' of the early 20th century when Siglufjörður was the herring capital of the North Atlantic. Explore interactive exhibits, restored boats, and period-accurate salt-fish processing facilities.
day_by_day.evening: Aurora watching from the Siglufjörður harbour or hillside. The town's extreme northern latitude (66°N — just inside the Arctic Circle) and minimal light pollution make it one of Iceland's premier aurora-viewing locations. Hotel Siglunes can arrange a local guide with a 4WD to drive to optimal dark-sky viewpoints above the fjord.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes breakfast — fresh pastries, Icelandic yoghurt, smoked lamb, and strong coffee
meals.lunch: Kaffi Rauðka in Siglufjörður — a cosy local café serving fish soup, open-faced sandwiches, and homemade cakes
meals.dinner: Private in-hotel dinner or Sigló Hótel's restaurant — pan-seared cod with butter sauce, roasted root vegetables, and Icelandic schnapps (Brennivín)

day_by_day.notes: January sunrise in Siglufjörður is around 11:00 and sunset around 15:30 — only about 4.5 hours of daylight. Plan outdoor activities around this window. Dress in multiple thermal layers; windproof and waterproof outer shell essential. KP index forecasts available at vedur.is for aurora planning.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Hofsós, a charming village 45 minutes south of Siglufjörður on the eastern shore of the Skagafjörður fjord. Visit the Icelandic Emigration Centre — a world-class museum documenting the mass emigration of Icelanders to North America in the late 19th century. The building itself is a beautifully restored 18th-century warehouse. Explore the tiny village and its photogenic harbour.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the Hofsós Geothermal Swimming Pool — arguably Iceland's most scenically situated public pool, perched on a cliff edge with panoramic views over Skagafjörður and the mountains of the Tröllaskagi peninsula. Soak in the infinity-edge hot tubs with views that rival any luxury spa in the world. Return to Siglufjörður by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at Hotel Siglunes. Enjoy the hotel's common areas and fjord views. If the sky clears, step outside for aurora watching directly from the hotel terrace — the fjord setting provides beautiful reflections of the northern lights on calm water nights.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes — skyr with Icelandic honey, rye bread with smoked salmon, fresh fruit
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet lunch from Hotel Siglunes to enjoy at Hofsós, or light refreshments at the Emigration Centre café
meals.dinner: Hotel Siglunes in-house dinner — request a special chef's tasting menu featuring local Skagafjörður lamb and Arctic char (arrange in advance)

day_by_day.notes: The Hofsós pool is open year-round but hours may be limited in winter — confirm opening times before departure. The drive between Siglufjörður and Hofsós via the Héðinsfjörður tunnel and Route 76 is spectacular in winter. Road conditions permitting, the coastal route offers dramatic sea-cliff scenery.

day_by_day.morning: Guided ice fishing experience on one of the frozen lakes near Siglufjörður with a local expert. Drill through the ice, drop lines for Arctic char and trout, and experience a quintessentially Icelandic winter tradition. Your guide provides all equipment, warm shelters, and hot drinks. Duration approximately 3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Siglufjörður town at leisure. Visit the local art gallery and browse the small but characterful shops along the main street. Stop at the old ski lodge area — Siglufjörður has a small ski area (Skarðsdalur) that operates in winter; enquire about a private ski or snowboard session if conditions allow. Alternatively, enjoy a private yoga or wellness session arranged through the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Premium aurora photography workshop with a local professional photographer. Head to pre-scouted dark-sky locations above the fjord with tripods and camera equipment provided. Learn long-exposure techniques to capture the aurora borealis. Even if aurora activity is low, the Milky Way and star photography in this remote location is extraordinary.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes — full hot breakfast with eggs, Icelandic sausages, and freshly baked bread
meals.lunch: Kaffi Rauðka — warming lamb soup and freshly baked cinnamon rolls
meals.dinner: Sigló Hótel Restaurant — five-course tasting menu with wine pairing; dishes feature locally sourced Skagafjörður ingredients

day_by_day.notes: Ice fishing is weather and ice-thickness dependent — your hotel concierge can confirm conditions. The photography workshop is best booked through local operators such as Arctic Adventures or a Siglufjörður-based guide. Bring hand warmers and a fully charged camera battery (cold drains batteries rapidly).

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to Akureyri — Iceland's 'Capital of the North' and the country's second-largest city, approximately 1 hour south of Siglufjörður via the scenic Route 82 and Route 1. Depart by private vehicle after breakfast. Upon arrival, visit the iconic Akureyrarkirkja church perched on a hill above the city, then explore the charming pedestrianised Hafnarstræti street with its boutiques and galleries.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Akureyri Botanical Garden (Lystigarðurinn) — the world's northernmost botanical garden, beautiful even in winter with its snow-covered structures. Then head to the Akureyri Art Museum for rotating exhibitions of Icelandic contemporary art. In the late afternoon, visit the Sundlaug Akureyrar geothermal pool complex — a beloved local institution with multiple hot tubs and a large outdoor pool.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Akureyri before the return drive to Siglufjörður. Akureyri has a surprisingly sophisticated dining scene for a city of 20,000 people. Return to hotel by 21:00–22:00.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes — continental and hot breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Rub23 Restaurant, Akureyri — celebrated for its creative sushi and Icelandic fusion cuisine; Arctic char sashimi and langoustine rolls
meals.dinner: Strikið Restaurant, Akureyri — rooftop views over the fjord, premium Icelandic lamb fillet and lobster bisque with local craft beer

day_by_day.notes: The drive from Siglufjörður to Akureyri via Route 82 passes through the Ólafsfjörður tunnel and offers stunning fjord scenery. In January, allow extra time for potential icy road sections. Akureyri is a worthwhile full-day destination — consider an optional whale-watching or dog-sledding excursion if time permits.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning at Hotel Siglunes. Sleep in, enjoy a leisurely breakfast, and take a slow morning walk along the Siglufjörður harbour front. Watch local fishing boats and enjoy the extraordinary stillness of the fjord in winter. The mountains surrounding the town are often dusted with fresh snow overnight — a perfect photography opportunity in the soft morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided horse riding excursion on Icelandic horses — the unique, pure-bred Icelandic breed known for its smooth 'tölt' gait. A local farm near Siglufjörður or Sauðárkrókur offers winter riding experiences through snow-covered lava fields and along fjord-side trails. Duration approximately 2 hours. Icelandic horses are exceptionally sure-footed in winter conditions.
day_by_day.evening: Private in-hotel spa evening. Arrange for a massage therapist to visit the hotel (many Icelandic hotels can arrange this), or enjoy a long soak in any available hot tub. If skies are clear, this is an excellent night for aurora watching from the hotel — set an alarm for 22:00–02:00 when aurora activity peaks.

meals.breakfast: Extended leisurely breakfast at Hotel Siglunes — fresh pastries, smoked fish platter, Icelandic cheeses, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the hotel or Kaffi Rauðka — open-faced sandwiches with gravlax and capers
meals.dinner: Private chef dinner at Hotel Siglunes — arrange in advance for a bespoke multi-course meal featuring the day's freshest local catch and Skagafjörður lamb

day_by_day.notes: This is a deliberate slower-paced day to avoid travel fatigue mid-trip. Horse riding farms in the area include Lýtingsstaðir and Hestasport near Varmahlíð — book at least 48 hours in advance. Icelandic horses are gentle and suitable for all experience levels.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Skagafjörður region — one of Iceland's most historically rich and scenically dramatic fjords. Depart after breakfast by private 4WD. Visit Glaumbær Turf Farm (if not visited on Day 2) — a UNESCO-listed cluster of traditional Icelandic turf houses dating to the 18th century, offering an intimate glimpse into pre-modern Icelandic life. The snow-covered turf roofs in winter are extraordinarily photogenic.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Varmahlíð and the Víðimýri Turf Church — one of Iceland's best-preserved medieval turf churches, dating to 1834 but built on a site of worship going back to the Saga Age. Nearby, visit a local sheep farm for a behind-the-scenes look at Icelandic farming traditions. In winter, the sheep are kept indoors in traditional stone barns — a fascinating and authentic experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður by late afternoon. Enjoy a quiet evening with dinner at the hotel. If aurora forecasts are favourable (KP index 3+), arrange a late-night aurora drive with a local guide to elevated viewpoints above the fjord.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes — hot porridge with Icelandic cream and berries, smoked lamb, fresh juice
meals.lunch: Hótel Varmahlíð restaurant — hearty Icelandic lamb stew and freshly baked rye bread in a cosy farmhouse setting
meals.dinner: Hotel Siglunes or Sigló Hótel — grilled Arctic char with dill butter, roasted potatoes, and a glass of Icelandic craft gin

day_by_day.notes: Skagafjörður is known as Iceland's 'horse capital' — you may spot Icelandic horse herds roaming the snow-covered fields. The region is also famous for its Saga connections; Grettis Saga and Laxdæla Saga are set in this area. Pick up a copy from a local bookshop for evening reading.

day_by_day.morning: Guided glacier and mountain photography hike above Siglufjörður with a certified mountain guide. Ascend to a viewpoint above the town for panoramic views of the fjord, the surrounding Tröllaskagi peaks, and on clear days, the distant Snæfellsjökull glacier on the Snæfellsnes peninsula. The hike is moderate in difficulty and takes approximately 3 hours round trip. Crampons and poles provided.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to town and visit the Siglufjörður Folk Museum annex — a collection of restored early 20th-century buildings including a pharmacy, general store, and doctor's surgery, all preserved in period detail. Spend the remainder of the afternoon at leisure: read by the fire at the hotel, browse local craft shops, or simply watch the extraordinary winter light play across the fjord.
day_by_day.evening: Special aurora dinner experience: arrange with the hotel or a local operator to set up a private outdoor dining table (with heated tent or igloo structure) at a dark-sky location above the fjord. Dine on a curated menu of Icelandic delicacies under the stars — and potentially under the northern lights. This is a once-in-a-lifetime premium experience.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes — eggs Benedict with smoked salmon, fresh pastries, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Kaffi Rauðka — fish and chips Icelandic style with malt vinegar and tartar sauce
meals.dinner: Private outdoor aurora dining experience — catered by Hotel Siglunes or a local caterer; menu includes smoked lamb, langoustine, skyr panna cotta, and Icelandic schnapps

day_by_day.notes: The outdoor aurora dining experience requires advance planning (minimum 3–5 days) and is weather dependent. Have a backup indoor dinner plan. The mountain hike should only proceed with a certified guide in January — avalanche risk assessment is essential in this region. Check vedur.is for mountain weather forecasts.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Siglufjörður after breakfast for a scenic drive south toward the Snæfellsnes Peninsula — approximately 4.5 hours by private vehicle. En route, stop at Hvammstangi on the Vatnsnes Peninsula for a seal-watching excursion. The Icelandic Seal Centre provides context, and the nearby Illugastaðir farm is one of Iceland's best seal-watching spots, with hundreds of harbour seals hauled out on the rocks even in winter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue south to the Snæfellsnes Peninsula and check in at a luxury accommodation (pre-booked) near Stykkishólmur or Arnarstapi — such as Hótel Búðir, one of Iceland's most romantic and remote luxury hotels, set beside a 700-year-old lava field and black sand beach beneath the Snæfellsjökull glacier. Explore the immediate surroundings: the ancient Búðakirkja black church is a short walk away.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset (around 16:30) over the Snæfellsjökull glacier from Hótel Búðir — one of Iceland's most iconic winter views. The glacier glows pink and gold in the alpenglow. After dark, the remote location offers exceptional aurora viewing directly from the hotel grounds.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes — final breakfast; pack a gourmet picnic for the road
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic en route, or stop at Café Hvammstangi for fish soup and fresh bread
meals.dinner: Hótel Búðir Restaurant — one of Iceland's finest rural restaurants; locally sourced lamb, langoustine, and Snæfellsnes seafood with an extensive Icelandic wine list

day_by_day.notes: This is a transition day moving from the north to the Snæfellsnes Peninsula. The drive is long but extraordinarily scenic — the Vatnsnes Peninsula seal colony is a highlight not to be missed. Hótel Búðir should be booked well in advance as it has limited rooms and is extremely popular.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day exploration of the Snæfellsnes Peninsula — often called 'Iceland in miniature' for its concentration of diverse landscapes. Begin with a guided snowmobile or super-jeep tour onto the Snæfellsjökull glacier — the ice cap that Jules Verne used as the entrance to the Earth's core in 'Journey to the Centre of the Earth.' Explore ice caves, crevasses, and summit views (weather permitting) with a certified glacier guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend from the glacier and explore the dramatic southern coastline: visit Djúpalónssandur black pebble beach with its ancient lifting stones (traditional tests of fishermen's strength), the basalt sea stacks at Lóndrangar, and the bird cliffs at Arnarstapi where Arctic fulmars nest in the rock faces. The coastline is wild and elemental in January.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hótel Búðir for a luxurious evening. Enjoy a pre-dinner drink in the hotel bar — try an Icelandic craft gin and tonic with local botanicals. The hotel's remote location and minimal light pollution make it one of the best aurora-viewing spots in Iceland.

meals.breakfast: Hótel Búðir — full Icelandic breakfast with panoramic glacier views
meals.lunch: Packed premium lunch on the glacier or at Arnarstapi — thermos of hot soup, smoked lamb sandwiches, and Icelandic chocolate
meals.dinner: Hótel Búðir Restaurant — pan-seared halibut with lemon butter, Snæfellsnes lamb rack, and skyr cheesecake with crowberry compote

day_by_day.notes: Glacier tours on Snæfellsjökull must be booked with a certified guide — operators include Snjófell and Summit Adventure Guides. The glacier is accessible year-round but conditions vary; crampons and harnesses are provided. The Snæfellsjökull National Park visitor centre in Hellissandur has useful maps and information.

day_by_day.morning: Drive from Hótel Búðir back toward Reykjavik (approximately 2.5 hours) via the northern Snæfellsnes route through Grundarfjörður. Stop at Kirkjufell mountain — Iceland's most photographed peak, a dramatic arrow-shaped mountain rising from the sea. In winter, the mountain is often snow-capped and the nearby Kirkjufellsfoss waterfall may be partially frozen — a spectacular scene. Allow 1 hour for photography.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Reykjavik by early afternoon. Check in to a luxury Reykjavik hotel (such as The Retreat at Blue Lagoon, Hotel Borg, or ION Adventure Hotel). Spend the afternoon at Laugardalslaug Geothermal Pool — Reykjavik's largest public geothermal pool complex with multiple hot tubs, steam rooms, and a large outdoor pool. This is where locals come to relax and socialise — an authentic Icelandic experience. Follow with a visit to Hlemmur Mathöll food hall for artisan snacks and local produce.
day_by_day.evening: Final full evening in Iceland. Snorkeling or Diving in Silfra Fissure is not possible this evening (it's a daytime activity), so instead enjoy a premium Northern Lights Hunt from Reykjavik — a guided minibus tour with expert aurora chasers using real-time data to find the best viewing spots outside the city.

meals.breakfast: Hótel Búðir — final breakfast with glacier views before departure
meals.lunch: Hlemmur Mathöll food hall, Reykjavik — graze on Icelandic street food: lobster soup, lamb hot dogs, and fresh pastries from multiple artisan vendors
meals.dinner: Óx Restaurant, Reykjavik — an ultra-exclusive 12-seat counter restaurant with a single nightly tasting menu; one of Iceland's most coveted dining experiences (book months in advance)

day_by_day.notes: Kirkjufell is best photographed in the blue hour before sunrise (around 10:00–11:00) or at sunset (around 16:00). The mountain featured prominently in Game of Thrones — a popular reference point for fans. Óx Restaurant requires advance reservation and is operated by the same team as Grillmarkaðurinn; if unavailable, Grillmarkaðurinn itself is an excellent alternative.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Iceland. Rise early for the Golden Circle Day Tour — Iceland's most celebrated natural route. Depart Reykjavik by private vehicle at 08:00. First stop: Þingvellir National Park (UNESCO World Heritage Site) — walk the rift valley between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates, visit the ancient Alþingi parliament site, and if time and conditions allow, snorkel or dive in the crystal-clear Silfra Fissure (water temperature 2–4°C; dry suits provided). This is one of the world's top diving experiences.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Golden Circle: visit the Geysir Geothermal Area where the Strokkur geyser erupts every 5–8 minutes to heights of 20–30 metres — a reliable and dramatic natural spectacle. Then proceed to Gullfoss Waterfall — the 'Golden Falls,' a thundering two-tiered cascade that partially freezes in winter, creating extraordinary ice formations. Return to Reykjavik by 16:00 for final packing and hotel checkout.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to Keflavik International Airport by private luxury vehicle (approximately 45 minutes from Reykjavik). Allow 2.5–3 hours before departure for check-in and security. Enjoy a final Icelandic meal at the airport's premium lounge or restaurant before boarding.

meals.breakfast: Luxury Reykjavik hotel — full hot breakfast before the early departure
meals.lunch: Friðheimar Greenhouse Restaurant near Geysir — a unique dining experience inside a working tomato greenhouse; tomato soup, tomato bruschetta, and tomato-based cocktails (all grown on-site)
meals.dinner: Keflavik Airport premium lounge or Duus Restaurant in Keflavik town (if time allows) — smoked lamb, Icelandic fish stew, and a farewell glass of Brennivín schnapps

day_by_day.notes: The Silfra snorkeling experience requires advance booking (minimum 24–48 hours) and is weather/water-level dependent. Operators include DIVE.IS and Arctic Adventures. Participants must be comfortable swimmers; no diving certification required for snorkeling. The dry suit keeps you warm but the water is extremely cold — an unforgettable experience. Ensure all luggage is packed the night before for an efficient morning departure.
